blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Large language models (LLMs) are expanding from assisting scientific research and engineering to autonomously developing and improving AI systems, advancing AI for AI (AI4AI) as a pathway toward recursive self-improvement (RSI). Workflow-driven machine learning engineering (MLE) systems provide a practical path toward this pursuit through complex orchestration that manages long-horizon experimentation, while recent MLE systems adopt model-directed interaction, allowing models to autonomously organize experiments and adapt optimization strategies based on execution feedback. However, feedback from each experiment reflects several preceding decisions, and a long MLE run contains many such costly experiments. Training must therefore select useful supervision from long interaction trajectories and learn from intermediate outcomes. We propose a post-training method for autonomous long-horizon MLE optimization and apply it to train MLExpert, a 35B Mixture-of-Experts agentic model. We design the Kaggle-MLE Factory to construct executable tasks and an interaction harness for model-directed experimentation. Hierarchical agentic SFT transfers general tool-use and coding capabilities to MLE through outcome-guided supervision. Windowed Interaction RL (WIRL) treats the multi-turn decisions between successive experiment results as an execution window and assigns it a shared outcome-based reward. Asynchronous collection and policy correction support policy updates before the trajectory ends. On MLE-Bench Lite, MLExpert improves the average medal rate of the base model from 37.9% to 72.7%, achieving performance comparable to larger frontier models such as Kimi-K3 and GLM-5.3. Further experiments show that MLExpert improves performance on NatureBench Lite, agent scaffold optimization, and algorithm optimization, suggesting that the learned optimization capability generalizes to other tasks.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
The rapid advancement of reasoning, code generation, and tool interaction in large language models (LLMs) is enabling artificial intelligence (AI) to move beyond assisting scientific research and engineering toward autonomously developing and improving AI systems.
These efforts include model training, optimization of solver programs, and algorithm design, making AI for AI (AI4AI) a research direction toward recursive self-improvement (RSI).
In this context, machine learning engineering (MLE) provides a concrete setting for this goal, requiring long-horizon optimization through repeated execution, feedback analysis, and revision rather than one-shot generation.
blocks.zh:
大型语言模型(LLMS)的推理,代码生成和工具交互的快速进步,使得人工智能(AI)超越了协助科学研究和工程,走向自主地发展和改进AI系统.
这些努力包括模式培训、优化解答程序以及算法设计,使AI(AI4AI)成为向递归自我改进(RSI)的研究方向.
在这方面,机器学习工程(MLE)为这一目标提供了具体的设定,需要通过反复执行,反馈分析,以及修正而不是一发一发来优化视野.

blocks.en:
Most existing MLE systems [ 1 , 2 , 3 ] extend code generation into iterative optimization through search, memory, or multi-agent collaboration.
As shown in Figure 1 (a), predefined workflows or search rules typically control experiment sequencing and stage transitions, while LLMs primarily generate or debug code at designated steps.
These systems rely heavily on manually designed control logic to organize long-horizon experimentation.
blocks.zh:
大多数现有的MLE系统[1,2,3]通过搜索,内存,或多代理协作,将代码生成扩展为迭代优化.
如图1 (a)所示,预定义的工作流程或搜索规则通常为控制实验测序和相位过渡,而LLMS则主要在指定步骤下生成或调试代码.
这些系统严重依赖人工设计的控制逻辑来组织长视距实验.

blocks.en:
Recently, Arbor [ 4 ] and Argus [ 5 ] maintain persistent research states and allow models to design, continue, and revise experiments, placing greater demands on the model’s ability to plan experiments and sustain optimization over long interaction horizons.
ML-Agent [ 6 ] combines multi-turn demonstrations with single-step RL, while Frontis-MA1 [ 7 ] trains program evolution operators through SFT and RL and integrates them into an external evolutionary search framework.
These approaches primarily train models for single-step decisions or local operations within externally organized processes.
In contrast, we study how to train models to organize experiments and improve solutions over sustained interaction, using experience and execution feedback from real-world MLE tasks.
However, training this long-horizon optimization capability poses three challenges.
1) Open-ended MLE requires an interaction environment that preserves experimental states while leaving action selection to the model.
2) High-quality long-horizon supervision is difficult to obtain because MLE tasks are heterogeneous and interaction trajectories may mix useful exploration and failure recovery with degraded decisions.
3) Each costly experiment returns feedback on several preceding decisions before the full run ends; online RL must use this intermediate signal while handling policy mismatch during asynchronous collection.
blocks.zh:
最近,Arbor [4] 和 Argus [5] 保持了持续的研究状态,并允许模型设计,继续并修改实验,对模型在长期互动视野上规划实验和维持优化的能力提出了更大的要求.
ML-Agent [6]将多转弯演示与单步RL结合,而Frontis-MA1 [7]通过SFT和RL训练程序演化操作员,并将其纳入外部演化搜索框架.
这些办法主要是在外部组织的进程内培训单步骤决定或当地业务的模式。
相形之下,我们研究如何利用来自现实世界的MLE任务的经验和执行反馈来训练模型来组织实验和改进解决方案,而不是持续的相互作用.
然而,这种长期优化能力的培训提出了三个挑战。
1) 开放式的 MLE 需要一个互动环境,既能保留实验状态,又能将动作选择留给模型.
2) 很难获得高质量的长视距监督,因为劳动与就业部的任务各不相同,相互作用的轨迹可能将有益的勘探和故障恢复与退化的决定相混合。
3)每个昂贵的实验在全部运行结束前返回对之前数个决定的反馈;在线RL必须使用这个中间信号,同时在同步收集时处理策略不匹配.

blocks.en:
To address these challenges, we propose a post-training method for autonomous MLE that combines a model-directed long-horizon interaction harness, hierarchical agentic SFT, and Windowed Interaction Reinforcement Learning (WIRL).
Based on this, we train MLExpert , a 35B Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) agentic model, to learn long-horizon optimization strategies.
As shown in Figure 1 (b), MLExpert uses sustained tool interaction within the interaction harness to autonomously organize experiments, revise solutions based on execution feedback, and maintain submission candidates.
We build the Kaggle-MLE Factory to convert historical Kaggle competitions into executable MLE tasks.
Hierarchical agentic SFT transfers general tool-use and coding capabilities to MLE optimization, with execution outcomes guiding the selection of trajectories and segments for supervision.
To use this intermediate feedback, WIRL treats each completed experiment as the boundary of an execution window containing decisions since the previous result. It trains those decisions with a shared outcome-based reward, while asynchronous collection and policy correction allow updates as trajectories continue.
On MLE-Bench Lite, MLExpert improves the average medal rate of the base model from 37.9% to 72.7%, achieving performance comparable to larger models such as Kimi-K3 and GLM-5.3.
MLExpert also improves performance on NatureBench Lite and transfers its optimization capabilities to agent scaffold and algorithm optimization tasks.
Our key contributions are:

以此为基础,我们培养出MLExpert,一种35B的混合-专家(MoE)代理模型,来学习长视距优化策略.
如图1(b)所示,MLExpert在互动利用范围内使用持续的工具互动,自主组织实验,根据执行反馈修改解决方案,并保留提交候选人.
我们建造了Kaggle-MLE工厂,将历史的Kaggle比赛转化为可执行的MLE任务.

要使用这种中间反馈,WIRL将每一个已完成的实验作为自上一个结果以来包含决定的执行窗口的边界. 它以共同的成果奖励来培训这些决定,同时同步收集和纠正政策,随着轨迹的不断更新。

blocks.en: 3.1 Kaggle-MLE Factory: Constructing Executable MLE Tasks
blocks.zh: 3.1 卡格-MLE 工厂:构建可执行的 MLE 任务

blocks.en:
Long-horizon Agentic MLE training requires executable tasks covering diverse data modalities, objectives, and domains.
Historical Kaggle competitions provide a rich source of real-world MLE problems, but their heterogeneous data organization, submission formats, and evaluation protocols make manual task adaptation difficult to scale.
Therefore, we build the Kaggle-MLE Factory, which converts historical competitions into executable tasks with a public workspace, a hidden test split, and a unified evaluation interface.
The Factory uses a multi-agent pipeline for task construction, validation, and repair.
The discovery agent filters competitions by status, scale, and submission format.
After competition data, leaderboard information, and official descriptions are collected, the analyzer agent extracts data structures, fields, and modality characteristics to form a task specification.
The generator agent then prepares task data, constructs a held-out test split with hidden labels from the original labeled data, and implements the task-specific evaluator.
The task is executed on real data and iteratively repaired based on validator checks of data integrity, submission format, and evaluation behavior to produce valid executable tasks.
Standardized task packages support different MLE agent frameworks.
Final manual review excludes tasks with unresolved label or scoring issues before trajectory collection.
Appendix A details agent responsibilities and implementation.

blocks.en: 3.2 Interaction Harness for Long-Horizon MLE Optimization
blocks.zh: 3.2 长视线的相互作用 优化

blocks.en:
To support model-directed long-horizon MLE optimization, we design an interaction harness that follows ReAct-style loop [ 9 ] , leaving branch selection and optimization-path decisions to the model rather than an external search policy.
The harness stores experimental states in solution nodes, each containing candidate code, execution logs, and metadata. Parent-linked revisions form an experiment tree that the model can revisit and compare to decide whether to continue, backtrack, or change optimization direction.
The harness provides tools for solution analysis, code revision, experiment execution, history retrieval, and submission management.
The model launches candidate execution through execute_code and updates its submission candidate through update_answer .
The complete tool list and descriptions are provided in Appendix B .

绳子将实验状态储存在溶液节点,每个节点都包含候选代码,执行日志和元数据. 与父母相关的修改形成了一个实验树,模型可以重新审视并比较,以决定是否继续,回溯轨道,还是改变优化方向.
该工具为溶液分析、代码修订、实验执行、历史检索和提交管理提供了工具。

blocks.en: 4.1 Hierarchical Agentic SFT
blocks.zh: 4.1 分级代理SFT

blocks.en:
Long-horizon MLE optimization requires general tool-use, coding skills, and domain-specific decision making.
We therefore use two-stage hierarchical agentic SFT.
In the first stage, coding and tool-use trajectories from diverse agentic tasks are used to learn basic tool-use and code revision capabilities.
The second stage adopts teacher trajectories from MLE domain and literature-derived scientific tasks to improve algorithm design, experimental analysis, and iterative optimization.
blocks.zh:
Long-horison MLE优化需要一般的工具使用,编码技能,以及特定域的决策.
因此我们使用两阶段的分级代理SFT.
在第一阶段,通过各种代理任务的编码和工具使用轨迹来学习基本的工具使用和代码修订能力.
第二阶段采用来自MLE域的教师轨迹和由文献衍生的科学任务来改进算法设计,实验分析,并进行迭代优化.

Complementary MLE demonstrations. MLE adaptation data cover both task initialization and sustained optimization.
For trajectories whose first complete solution executes successfully and reaches a quality threshold, we extract the interaction prefix from task start through the corresponding execution feedback as an initial-solution trajectory , typically covering task understanding, algorithm design, and code generation.
We also use long-horizon optimization trajectories from complete interactions, covering solution construction, feedback analysis, iterative revision, and final submission selection.
In addition, analysis sub-agent trajectories are adopted to train the model for independent data analysis and result diagnosis.

此外,还采用了分析子剂轨迹来培训独立数据分析和结果诊断模型.

blocks.en:
Outcome-guided supervision selection. Long-horizon MLE trajectories can contain effective exploration and failure recovery, but may also include misguided decisions or continued degradation after reaching a strong solution.
Therefore, we use execution results of submitted solutions to select high-quality trajectories and the segments used for supervision.
For trajectories that pass a quality threshold, we identify the first best-performing submission and measure the subsequent performance degradation.
When the post-peak degradation exceeds a threshold, we use the first best-performing submission as the anchor for retaining a trajectory prefix; otherwise, we use the last submission. The prefix ends at a complete tool-interaction boundary near the anchor.
This removes degraded tails while preserving useful exploration and failure recovery before the peak.

blocks.zh: 4.2 窗口互动强化学习

blocks.en:
Building on SFT, we further optimize the long-horizon decision policy using execution feedback from the model’s own exploration.
In MLE, solution quality is available only after training and evaluation, and each result depends on multiple rounds of analysis, code revision, and tool interaction.
We introduce Windowed Interaction RL (WIRL), which groups consecutive model decisions made between successive experiment results into an execution window u m u_{m} .
Each window is conditioned on the accumulated interaction history and associated with the outcome of the corresponding experiment launched through the execute_code tool (Sec. 3.2 ). The first window starts from the initial task state.
This allows policy updates to use feedback from completed experiments without waiting for the entire task trajectory to finish.

blocks.en: Harness

blocks.en:
MLExpert achieves the highest medal rate among same-scale models and reaches the performance level of larger frontier models. As shown in Table 1 , under the unified MLExpert Harness, MLExpert raises the medal rate of its Qwen3.6-35B-A3B base model from 37.9% to 72.7%, achieving the highest rate among the same-scale models evaluated and performance comparable to GLM-5.3 and Kimi-K3.
These results show that long-horizon agentic post-training substantially improves the base model’s MLE capability, bringing a 35B model to a performance level comparable to larger frontier models.
blocks.zh:
MLExpert在同级模型中实现最高奖牌率,并达到较大前沿模型的性能水平. 如表1所示,在统一的MLExpert Harness下,MLExpert将它的Quen3.6-35B-A3B基型的奖牌率从37.9%提高到72.7%,在被评价的同级型号中实现了最高率,其性能与GLM-5.3和Kimi-K3相当.
这些结果显示,长相干剂的后期训练大大地提高了基模型的MLE能力,使35B模型达到与较大的前沿模型相媲美的性能水平.

blocks.en:
MLExpert retains its advantage over the base model under a general-purpose coding harness. With Claude Code, MLExpert achieves a 69.7% medal rate, compared with 42.4% for its base model, and exceeds the strongest evaluated same-scale baseline by 22.7 percentage points.

blocks.en: RL baselines and key WIRL design choices. We compare WIRL with trajectory-level GRPO and PPO-style optimization under the same MLE environment and MLE-SFT initialization. GRPO uses group-relative advantages, whereas PPO-style optimization uses a clipped objective weighted by terminal trajectory rewards without an additional critic. We also evaluate WIRL variants that remove the trend reward or policy correction separately. As shown in Table 4 , GRPO and PPO-style optimization achieve 56.1% and 60.6%, respectively, both below the 62.1% achieved by MLE-SFT, supporting WIRL’s overall design of learning from execution-window feedback. In contrast, the two WIRL variants reach 66.7% and 65.2%, respectively, while full WIRL further improves the medal rate to 72.7%, indicating that both the local trend reward and policy correction contribute to the final improvement. Further analysis in Appendix 10 shows that asynchronous execution-window collection reduces the learner waiting fraction compared with trajectory-based GRPO.

blocks.en: 6 Related work
blocks.zh: 6 相关工作

blocks.en: 6.1 Agents for Automated ML Research
blocks.zh: 6.1 自动ML研究代理商

blocks.en:
LLM agents increasingly automate data analysis, model development, and experimental iteration, with recent work extending to autonomous AI system design and improvement [ 27 ] .
AIDE [ 1 ] and MLE-STAR [ 2 ] improve candidate solutions through iterative search and refinement, while MLEvolve [ 28 ] and MARS [ 29 ] use structured tree- or graph-based search, memory, and planning to organize long-horizon experimentation.
R&D-Agent [ 3 ] studies multi-role collaboration, while InternAgent [ 30 ] and FM-Agent [ 31 ] extend autonomous AI research across machine learning, algorithm optimization, and engineering tasks.
Recent systems including Arbor [ 4 ] and Argus [ 5 ] maintain persistent research states and increase model control.
blocks.zh:
LLM代理越来越自动化的数据分析,模型开发,以及实验迭代,最近的工作扩展到了自主的AI系统设计和改进[27].
AIDE [1]和MLE-STAR [2]通过迭代搜索和完善来改进候选解决方案,而MLEvolve [28]和MARS [29]则使用结构化的以树或图表为基础的搜索,内存,并计划组织长视实验.
R&D-Agent [3]研究多作用协作,而InternAgent [30]和FM-Agent [31]将自主AI研究扩展至机器学习,算法优化,以及工程任务.
包括Arbor [4]和Argus [5]在内的近期系统保持了持续的研究状态并增加了模型控制.

blocks.en:
Recent work develops MLE capabilities by training models on interaction experience.
ML-Agent [ 6 ] combines multi-turn demonstrations with single-step RL, while RL for MLE Agents [ 32 ] , MLE-RL [ 33 ] , and AceGRPO [ 34 ] study online MLE training with execution feedback, asynchronous sampling, or intermediate trajectory states.
Learning to Ideate [ 35 ] trains models to generate algorithm improvement suggestions, whereas Frontis-MA1 [ 7 ] applies SFT and RL to program evolution operators and combines them through an external evolutionary framework.
These approaches primarily train individual interaction steps or local components of externally organized optimization workflows.
SandMLE [ 36 ] applies trajectory-wise on-policy RL in micro-scale synthetic MLE environments.
We train model-directed long-horizon interaction policies on real-world MLE tasks, with WIRL using execution windows to learn multi-turn decisions from delayed execution feedback under asynchronous updates.

近期的工作通过互动经验培训模式来发展多边环境教育的能力。
ML-Agent [6] 将多回合演示与单步RL结合,而为 MLE Agents [32], MLE-RL [33], AceGRPO [34] 学习在线 MLE 训练,并附有执行反馈,同步取样,或中间轨迹状态.
学习意向 [35] 训练模型生成算法改进建议,而Frontis-MA1 [7] 将SFT和RL应用于程序演化操作员,并通过外部演化框架将其组合.
这些方法主要培训个别互动步骤或外部组织优化工作流程的本地组成部分。
SandMLE [36] 在微尺度合成的 MLE 环境中采用轨迹性政策RL.
我们在现实世界的 MLE 任务上训练模型引导的长视野互动政策,WIRL 使用执行窗口从同步更新下的延迟执行反馈中学习多回合决定.

blocks.en: 6.2 Post-Training Long-Horizon Agentic Models
blocks.zh: 6.2 培训后长效模型

blocks.en:
Recent research has increasingly focused on post-training agentic models for sustained interaction, complex tool use, and long-horizon decision making.
SWE-Gym [ 37 ] trains coding agents using trajectories collected from executable environments, while Search-R1 [ 38 ] and WebRL [ 39 ] learn multi-turn tool use from environment feedback and outcome rewards.
AgentFlow [ 40 ] directly optimizes planning policies in general multi-turn agentic interaction and uses trajectory-level outcomes to train intermediate decisions. Recent work has also explored generalist agentic models for long-horizon interaction.
Agents-A1 [ 41 ] uses long-horizon knowledge-action trajectories and multi-stage training, together with multi-teacher on-policy distillation (OPD), to combine capabilities from multiple domain teachers into a unified model.
Ornith-1.5 [ 14 ] extends self-scaffolding by jointly optimizing task generation, scaffold construction, and solution rollouts through RL.

最近的研究越来越注重培训后的代理模式,以促进持续互动、复杂的工具使用和长期决策。

AgentFlow [40]直接优化了一般多回合代理互动的规划政策,并使用轨迹级结果来训练中间决策. 近期的工作还探索了长相互动的通论剂模型.

blocks.en: 7 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 7 结论

blocks.en:
In this work, we introduce MLExpert, a 35B MoE agentic model trained to autonomously conduct and improve machine learning experiments over long interaction horizons.
We build an automated MLE task factory and a model-directed interaction harness, and train MLExpert with hierarchical agentic SFT and WIRL to learn from teacher demonstrations and execution feedback collected from its own exploration.
Extensive experiments show that MLExpert improves over its base model on MLE-Bench Lite and achieves performance comparable to larger frontier models.
Further improvements on NatureBench Lite and in agent scaffold and algorithm optimization demonstrate cross-task generalization.
These results support treating long-horizon optimization decision making as a trainable model capability, providing a practical path toward autonomous machine learning engineering and scientific experimentation.
blocks.zh:
在这部作品中,我们引入了MLExpert,一种35B的MOE代理模型,经过培训,可以自主地进行并改进长时间相互作用的机器学习实验.
我们建造了一个自动化的MILE任务工厂和一个模型导向的交互控制装置,并用分级代理SFT和WIRL培训MLExpert,学习教师演示和从自己的探索中收集的执行反馈.
广泛的实验显示,MLExpert在MLE-Bench Lite上改进了基础模型,并实现了与更大的前沿模型相类似的性能.
对Nature Bench Lite和代理脚手架和算法优化的进一步改进显示了跨任务概括化.
这些成果支持将长相优化决策作为一种可训练的模型能力,为自主机器学习工程和科学实验提供了一条实用的道路.

blocks.en:
We begin with a Meta-Kaggle 1 1 1 https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/kaggle/meta-kaggle competition metadata snapshot containing 11,649 entries.
Guided by the task-selection principles of MLE-bench [ 8 ] , the discovery agent considers task relevance, data availability, and the feasibility of offline evaluation.
Automated initial screening uses competition completion, at least 50 participating teams, and a dataset size limit of 200 GB as default criteria, checks submission-interface compatibility, and consults an exclusion list of existing tasks.
The agent further selects candidates across domains and data modalities, including vision, text, audio, tabular data, and time series.

The downloader and scraper retrieve competition data, official descriptions, and leaderboard information.
The analyzer agent extracts data structures, field information, and modality characteristics to form a task specification, which the generator agent uses to produce data-preparation and scoring code.
When test labels are unavailable, the pipeline constructs a held-out split from the original labeled data and keeps its labels on the evaluation side.
The executor runs generated task packages on real data, while the validator agent checks structural completeness, submission-format consistency, non-degenerate labels, train–test identifier overlap, and data availability.
The validator also executes the scoring function to check that it produces a valid score.
Execution and validation errors are returned to the construction agents for repair.
We conduct a final human review of the 160 registered tasks, excluding six with unresolved label or scoring-implementation issues and retaining 154 tasks for subsequent trajectory collection.

blocks.en: C.1 Details of Hierarchical Agentic SFT

blocks.en:
Training data sources.
The first SFT stage uses general coding and tool-use trajectories from StepFun [ 22 ] , while the second stage combines MLE teacher trajectories with literature-derived scientific trajectories. The MLE tasks comprise 154 tasks constructed by the Kaggle-MLE Factory and 134 tasks selected from MLE-Dojo [ 23 ] , with competitions overlapping with MLE-Bench removed. Following the task-construction approach of NatureBench [ 12 ] , we construct scientific experimentation tasks from 164 papers published in Nature-family journals, covering biology, materials science, physics, chemistry, and medicine, among other fields. The data used in these scientific tasks do not overlap with the NatureBench evaluation set. MLE teacher trajectories are generated by GLM-5.2 [ 42 ] , while scientific experimentation trajectories are generated by GLM-5.2 and Qwen3.8-Max [ 43 ] .
blocks.zh:

blocks.en: D.2 NatureBench Lite
blocks.zh: D.2 自然奔驰液

blocks.en:
We use the ten-task NatureBench Lite subset listed by Frontis-MA1 [ 7 ] , with the S and M definitions from NatureBench [ 12 ] .
We follow the official NatureBench evaluation protocol, with a four-hour runtime budget per task that excludes time spent scoring submissions.
Following NatureBench, we compute the normalized relative gap for each evaluation instance by subtracting the paper-reported SOTA value from the agent’s primary metric value, adjusting the sign so that improvements are positive, and dividing by the absolute SOTA value.
Instances without a valid submission receive a gap of − 1 -1 .
The task-level score g g is the mean gap across instances.
Match-SOTA and Surpass-SOTA report the percentages of tasks with g ≥ 0 g\geq 0 and g > 0.1 g>0.1 , respectively.
We report a single evaluation of MLExpert over the ten tasks, with Surpass-SOTA on five tasks and Match-SOTA on seven tasks, corresponding to 50.0% and 70.0%, respectively.
DeepSeek-V4-Pro Preview and MiniMax M3 [ 17 ] results are taken from Table 2 of Frontis-MA1.
Our NatureBench evaluations use NVIDIA H200 GPUs; external reference results retain their original evaluation conditions.

我们使用Frontis-MA1 [7] 列出的"十大任务"(Nature Bench Lite)子集,其中S和M的定义来自"Nature Bench [12]".
我们遵循Nature Bench的正式评价协议,每项任务都有4小时的运行时间预算,不包括花在评分上的时间。
沿着"自然奔驰"(Nature Bench),我们计算每个评价实例的正态相对差距,方法是从代理商的主要度量值中减去所报的纸质SOTA值,调整标志以便改进为正值,并除以绝对SOTA值.
未提交有效材料的事例的差额为− 1 - 1。
任务级别得分g是各种实例之间的平均差距。
Match-SOTA 和 Surpass-SOTA 分别报告 g = 0 g\ geq 0 和 g > 0.1 g> 0.1 的任务百分比。
我们报告对MLExpert对十项任务的单一评价,Surpass-SOTA对五项任务,Match-SOTA对七项任务,分别为50.0%和70.0%。
DeepSeek-V4-Pro预览和MiniMax M3[17]结果取自Frontis-MA1表2.
我们的"自然奔驰"评价使用NVIDIA H200 GPU;外部参考结果保留了最初的评价条件.

blocks.en:

Compared with Nex-N2.5-mini, MLExpert has a higher Surpass-SOTA rate, 50.0% versus 20.0%, but a lower Match-SOTA rate, 70.0% versus 80.0%.
MLExpert more frequently exceeds the reference by the Surpass-SOTA margin, while Nex matches the reference on a larger fraction of evaluations.
MLExpert matches the 50.0% Surpass-SOTA rate of GLM-5.3, whose Match-SOTA rate is higher at 90.0%.

与Nex-N2.5-mini相比,MLExpert的Surpass-SOTA率较高,50.0%对20.0%,但Match-SOTA率较低,70.0%对80.0%.

blocks.en: D.3 AIME Agent Scaffold Optimization
blocks.zh: D.3 AIME代理脚手架优化

blocks.en:
The outer model optimizes a Python agent scaffold that calls a fixed gpt-4.1-nano-2025-04-14 solver.
All optimizers start from the same single-query scaffold and share the task environment, tools, and evaluator.
Each search has a four-hour time limit and a maximum of 1,000 interaction steps, with a context limit of 200,000 tokens and an output limit of 65,536 tokens per step.
The scaffold can modify prompting, calling, verification, voting, and answer-extraction procedures, with at most ten inner-model calls per problem.
Initial uses one solver call, while Majority@5 takes a majority vote over five independently sampled answers.
blocks.zh:
外型优化了一种叫固定gpt-4.1-nano-2025-04-14解决器的Python代理脚手架.
所有优化者都从同一个单克脚手架开始,共享任务环境,工具,以及评价者.
每次搜索都有4小时的时间限制并最多有1000个互动步骤,上下文限制为20万个令牌,每步输出限制为65,536个令牌.
脚手架可以修改提示,调用,核实,投票,和答取程序,每个问题最多可以有十个内型调用.
最初使用一个解答调用,而Mority@5则对五个独立抽样的答案进行多数投票.

blocks.en:
Development uses all 30 problems from AIME 2025, with three evaluations per problem for each candidate scaffold.
The outer model receives aggregate accuracy, call counts, and sanitized error summaries.
Exact-request response caching is used during development to reuse inner-solver responses to identical requests.
After search, the selected scaffold is frozen and evaluated using fresh solver calls on AIME 2023, 2024, and 2026.
Each held-out year contains 30 problems and is evaluated three times; these years provide no feedback for scaffold development or selection.
Thus, each optimizer contributes one frozen scaffold, with three evaluation repetitions per year.
blocks.zh:
开发使用了AIME 2025的所有30个问题,每个候选人脚手架每个问题有3个评价.
外出模型接收集合精度,调用计数,并进行消毒错误摘要.
在开发过程中使用了精确请求响应缓存来再利用对相同请求的内解响应.
搜索后,被选中的脚手架被冷冻并使用新鲜的解析器调用AIME 2023,2024,和2026进行评估.
每个被搁置的年份有30个问题,经过三次评估;这些年没有为脚手架的开发或选择提供反馈.
因此,每个优化器都贡献出一个被冻结的脚手架,每年重复三次评价.

blocks.en:

blocks.en:
Solver-call efficiency after SFT. The scaffold optimized by MLExpert-SFT achieves 38.1% held-out accuracy with 3.51 solver calls per problem, approaching the 40.0% achieved by Kimi-K3 with approximately 59% fewer calls.
It also outperforms Majority@5, which reaches 24.8% with five calls per problem.
MLExpert-SFT therefore improves held-out accuracy over fixed majority voting while using fewer solver calls, suggesting that its optimized scaffold uses the solver more effectively.
These results indicate that SFT already supports effective scaffold optimization across held-out years.
blocks.zh:
SFT之后的解调效率. 由MLExpert-SFT优化的脚手架实现了38.1%的悬停精度,每个问题有3.51个解调器呼叫,接近Kimi-K3实现的40.0%,约59%的接通量减少.
它的表现也超过了多数人@5,达到24.8%,每个问题有五次通话。
因此,MLExpert-SFT在使用较少的解析器呼叫的同时,比固定多数表决提高了被搁置的准确性,表明其优化的脚手架更有效地使用解析器.
这些结果显示,SFT已经支持跨被扣留年份的有效脚手架优化.

blocks.en:
Further gains from WIRL. WIRL raises held-out accuracy from 38.1% to 43.7%, a gain of 5.6 percentage points, with improvements on all three held-out years.
The resulting scaffold uses 8.40 calls per problem, compared with 3.51 for MLExpert-SFT and 8.65 for Kimi-K3.
With a similar number of calls to Kimi-K3, MLExpert exceeds its 40.0% accuracy, while GLM-5.3 achieves 48.1% with 9.39 calls.
The SFT and RL results therefore offer different accuracy–call trade-offs: SFT yields an effective scaffold with fewer calls, while further RL finds a more accurate scaffold that uses more calls.
blocks.zh:
进一步从WIRL获得收益. WIRL将被扣留的准确度从38.1%提高到43.7%,提高了5.6个百分点,所有三个被扣留年份都有所改善。
由此产生的脚手架每个问题使用8.40个呼叫,而MLExpert-SFT则使用3.51个,而Kimi-K3则使用8.65个.
由于与Kimi-K3的通话次数相近,MLExpert的准确度已超过40.0%,而GLM-5.3则以9.39的通话达到48.1%.
因此,SFT和RL结果提供了不同的准确性-调用权衡: SFT产生一个有效的脚手架,较少的呼叫,而更进一步的RL发现一个使用更多呼叫的更准确的脚手架.
